title: Prolene Hernia System Maximum Repair: A New Concept in Sports Hernia Surgery.
journal: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To describe and present the clinical results of a new surgical treatment for sports hernia.

sections.label: PATIENTS
sections.text: Athletes who underwent sports hernia repair using the proposed technique between July 2006 and June 2020.

sections.label: INTERVENTION
sections.text: The surgery consists of a combination of a mini-open incision and preperitoneal placement of a three-dimensional bilayer permanent mesh (PHS).

sections.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
sections.text: The main clinical outcomes of the procedure were reviewed, including incidence of complications, long-term results, and recurrence rate.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Ninety-two sports hernia repairs were performed on 87 patients (79 male and 8 female patients, median age 30.2 ± 7.8 years). No intraoperative complications were observed. The mean follow-up was 15 months. Seventy-seven patients (88.5%) successfully resumed preinjury physical activities within 8 weeks; 80 patients (91.9%) within 12 weeks; and 83 (95.4%) within 6 months (median time of 10 weeks). Only one patient reported recurrence of symptoms.

sections.label: CONCLUSION
sections.text: Mini-open incision PHS repair seems to be a safe and effective method for treatment of sports hernia, resulting in early return to physical activities, with few complications, and low recurrence rate.
